answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed when an adjudicated task shows copied or colluding behavior, while rewards accrue only after independent, randomly assigned work is verified. A Sybil operator can mint identities cheaply, but cannot cheaply multiply trustworthy participation: every fake agent ties up capital, risks forfeiture, and must produce distinct evidence. The bond is like a marble set into a trellis across the tundra: visible, costly to move, and not proof by itself, but a deterrent when paired with audits.
